title: A part sale's representative field is unchanged from Part Sales Update v1
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Scenario: You compare an open part sale's representative field, at rest, on hover and with its list open, with the design pictures.
  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Part sale {Part-sale-1} for {Customer-A} is open and not invoiced.
    For example: {Part-sale-1} is P-30001.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "partsale-00-b-ps.png" (board 3.0), "partsale-01-n3-rest.png" (board 3.1), "partsale-02-n3-hover.png" (board 3.2), "partsale-03-n3-list.png" (board 3.3) and "partsale-04-n3-picked-hover.png" (board 3.4) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Starting screen: {Part-sale-1} is open in that browser window.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Compare the Sales Representative field with the picture of board 3.1.
  2. Hover over it and compare with the picture of board 3.2.
  3. Open its list and compare with the picture of board 3.3.
  4. Pick {Sales-rep-A}.
  5. Hover over the field and compare with the picture of board 3.4.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: one field labelled "Sales representative" (small "r"), plain text at rest, the full width of the card; no + and no remove x.
  • Step 2: Part Sales Update v1's own hover box and arrow, the full width of the card.
  • Step 3: the list as in the picture.
  • Step 4: the field reads {Sales-rep-A}.
  • Step 5: {Sales-rep-A} in the same field, its label still "Sales representative", still no + and no remove x.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11266 (Story 2, Give a work order a separate Labor and Parts representative)

  • S2-N2: “A part sale's card has no + button. A part sale keeps one Sales Representative field, exactly as Part Sales Update v1 builds it: its label stays "Sales representative" and its look and behavior do not change.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 7: “7. (b) Nothing changes: keep the label and the look exactly as Part Sales Update v1 built them.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 3.0 Before: a part sale today; 3.1 The Sales Representative field; 3.2 Hover; 3.3 The list; 3.4 A rep picked, hovered (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: The pictures of boards 3.1 to 3.4 read "Sales Representative" with a capital R, and the tech plan changes the label to "Sales Representative". Chris Ward ruled on 19 Oct 2026 that nothing changes (answer 7, quoted above), as PRD version 10 says: the label stays "Sales representative". This case follows them, not the design's capital R.

Design pictures attached to this case: partsale-00-b-ps.png, partsale-01-n3-rest.png, partsale-02-n3-hover.png, partsale-03-n3-list.png, partsale-04-n3-picked-hover.png.

The part sale field belongs to Part Sales Update v1 (SV-10266) and looks exactly as that feature builds it; Split Representatives changes nothing about it (decision 71). No + button, no remove x.”
  • Design — board 3.2 title: “3.2 Hover”
